source_admission: Published values used in love_numbers.py, crustal_loading.py and the README's section on the crust's response to the water, each with how far it was read on 2026-11-04. The search was bounded to one radial interior model, the elastic thickness under the mare basins, the lunar mantle's viscosity and the sea-level equation's method. No outside dataset or full paper is committed. Values marked open are stated brackets that the reading did not settle.

interior_model.about: Category 4a medians of Briaud et al. 2023 (Table 4), with the crust and mantle of their Table 2, which follow Williams et al. 2014. Rigidity is the source's; it gives no compressional velocity (its ALMA code treats the Moon as incompressible). love_numbers.py carries the crust to the Moon's 1737.4 km and takes a Poisson solid (nu = 0.25) for the compressible case. Shear velocities implied: crust 2.43 km/s, mantle 4.41 km/s, low-viscosity zone 2.70 km/s.

sources.citation: Briaud A, Fienga A, Melini D, Rambaux N, Mémin A, Spada G, Saliby C, Hussmann H, Stark A, Viswanathan V, Baguet D 2023, Constraints on the lunar core viscosity from tidal deformation (arXiv:2301.04035v1, 10 January 2023)
sources.use: interior_model: layer radii, densities and rigidities; the mantle's adopted viscosity of 1e21 Pa s; the low-viscosity zone's radius, density and viscosity

low_viscosity_zone.abstract_constraint: radius 500 +/- 1 km, viscosity (4.5 +/- 0.8)e16 Pa s, density 3400 +/- 10 kg/m3

sources.citation: Turcotte DL, Willemann RJ, Haxby WF, Norberry J 1981, Role of membrane stresses in the support of planetary topography, Journal of Geophysical Research 86(B5), 3951-3959
sources.use: the thin elastic shell: deflection w_n = q_n a^4 (L - 1 + nu) / (D (L^3 - 4 L^2) + E Te a^2 (L - 2)), L = n(n + 1)
sources.access: equation as reproduced in later reviews; not reread. Checked in tests against a thick elastic shell over the same relaxed interior

sources.citation: Mascon flexure as reviewed by Solomon SC, Head JW 1980, Lunar mascon basins: lava filling, tectonics, and evolution of the lithosphere, Reviews of Geophysics 18, 107-141, and quoted by the GRAIL-era study of the Grimaldi basin (Icarus, 2017, ScienceDirect S0019103516304924); Variations in lunar elastic thickness from admittance spectral analysis, Icarus 403, 115631, 2023 (doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2023.115631)
sources.use: TE_CASES_M: flexure of the mare loads needs about 50 km under Serenitatis, Nectaris and Imbrium, 35 km under Crisium, 30 km under Humorum and Smythii and about 20 km under smaller basins, with 50-75 km under Imbrium in another analysis; GRAIL and LOLA admittance gives 13-72 km, mean 29 km, its reliable values away from the maria
sources.access: search summaries only, 2026-11-04: the mascon numbers as quoted there, without checking which of the two works each comes from; the 2023 admittance study's abstract as summarised (its authors not checked). Neither paper read. A GRAIL-era estimate under the nearside maria themselves was not found in the time allowed: open. These thicknesses record the lithosphere when the mare basalts loaded it, 3-3.8 billion years ago; today's colder lithosphere is likely thicker

sources.citation: Conventional moduli of lunar flexure studies (Young's modulus 100 GPa, Poisson's ratio 0.25)
sources.use: YOUNG_PA, POISSON: the shell's rigidity D = E Te^3 / 12 (1 - nu^2), so that a published Te gives the rigidity its study inferred
sources.access: design assumption: the usual values, not checked against the two Te sources (open). The interior's seismic rigidities give E of 40 GPa in the crust and 164 GPa in the mantle

sources.citation: Briaud et al. 2023 (above); Harada Y et al. 2014, Strong tidal heating in an ultralow-viscosity zone at the core-mantle boundary of the Moon, Nature Geoscience 7, 569-572 (doi:10.1038/ngeo2211)
sources.use: VISCOSITY_CASES_PA_S: the mantle under the lithosphere bracketed at 1e20-1e22 Pa s around the 1e21 adopted by Briaud et al.; the zone at the core's top near 2e16 Pa s (Harada et al.) to 4.5e16 (Briaud et al.)
sources.access: Harada et al.: abstract as summarised by search, 2026-11-04. The mantle bracket is open: the only value read is an Earth analogy, and the mascons' survival for billions of years says the cold upper mantle and lithosphere are stiffer still

sources.citation: Farrell WE, Clark JA 1976, On postglacial sea level, Geophysical Journal of the Royal Astronomical Society 46, 647-667; Mitrovica JX, Milne GA 2003, On post-glacial sea level: I. General theory, Geophysical Journal International 154, 253-267
sources.use: the method of crustal_loading.solve: the sea surface an equipotential of the deformed Moon and its water, the water thickness the sea surface less the deformed floor wherever positive, the volume or the area held by a uniform shift, iterated as the shoreline moves
sources.access: method as known; neither paper reread
